title: Kerfwise: Cut Planner

candidates.name: Cut List
candidates.why: Negative control: it is the repeated bare category phrase in the measured shelf and says nothing about the project-to-export workflow.

candidates.name: Kerfwise: Cut Planner
candidates.why: Kerf is a real cutting term and the job noun names planning rather than a generic calculator.

candidates.name: StockNest
candidates.why: It evokes arranging stock but loses cut-planning search language.

candidates.name: Cut Packet
candidates.why: It names the export but not the planning and optimisation work.

candidates.name: Kerfory
candidates.why: It is compact but its spelling and meaning are too opaque for a new listing.

rejected.name: CutList Optimizer
rejected.reason: It closely repeats the 1M+-install incumbent title and reduces the app to the optimisation feature rather than the distinct end-to-end woodworking workflow.

audience: A hobby woodworker or small-shop cabinet maker converting a furniture idea into parts, cuts, angles, material needs, and a workshop packet.
rationale: Kerfwise is a pronounceable cut-specific carrier paired with the planner job phrase, avoiding the incumbent's bare CutList title and the misleading implication that this is only a calculator.
collisionCheck: UNVERIFIED: exact-title and close-variant Play searches were not separately run, and USPTO, EUIPO/TMview, WIPO, and Russian class-9 registers were not searched; Play titles are not legal clearance.
localisationCheck: Kerfwise: Cut Planner is 21 characters; Kerfwise: план раскроя is 22 characters. Both are under the 30-character cap with at least five characters slack; Russian search quality requires native-speaker review.
